title: Acceptance-Controlled MIS-PO: Adaptive Trajectory Filtering for Stable Off-Policy RLVR Training

contributions.purpose: Identify what actually drives stability in off-policy RLVR trajectory filtering under high staleness.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation of trajectory filtering bound magnitudes in MIS-PO, isolating bound tightness from adaptive control.
contributions.evaluation: Tighter trajectory bounds that filter more aggressively yield +12.76 percentage points improvement over default MIS-PO bounds; bound magnitude is claimed as the primary driver.
contributions.source_quote: We identify that bound magnitude is the primary driver of stable off-policy RLVR training. Tighter trajectory bounds that filter more aggressively yield +12.76 percentage points improvement over default MIS-PO bounds.

contributions.purpose: Remove manual tuning of trajectory filtering bounds across staleness levels and training stages.
contributions.mechanism: AC-MIS-PO, an adaptive controller that targets a pre-specified acceptance rate schedule (40% permissive to 20% tightened) using quantile estimation with exponential moving average smoothing to set bound magnitudes automatically.
contributions.evaluation: The controller discovers appropriate bound magnitudes automatically while maintaining stable training under staleness s=256, where Fixed MIS-PO crashed at step 94 from gradient explosion.
contributions.source_quote: We propose AC-MIS-PO, an adaptive controller that targets acceptance rate using quantile estimation and EMA smoothing, automatically discovering appropriate bound magnitudes without manual tuning.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that acceptance-controlled filtering outperforms fixed-bound and variance-control baselines under high staleness.
contributions.mechanism: Comparison of AC-MIS-PO against Fixed MIS-PO, M2PO, and GRPO on mathematical reasoning benchmarks at staleness s=256.
contributions.evaluation: AC-MIS-PO achieves 32.57% average accuracy on Math500/AIME24/AIME25 versus Fixed MIS-PO (18.67%), M2PO (18.40%), and GRPO (6.57%) while maintaining training stability.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that AC-MIS-PO achieves 32.57% average accuracy on mathematical reasoning benchmarks (Math500, AIME24, AIME25) under staleness s = 256, outperforming Fixed MIS-PO (18.67%), M2PO (18.40%), and GRPO (6.57%) while maintaining training stability.

self_declared_provenance.quote: MIS-PO (Huang et al., 2026) applies binary accept/reject masks based on importance ratio bounds, filtering trajectories that deviate too far from the current policy. M2PO (Zheng et al., 2025b) constrains the second moment of importance ratios to control variance. However, these methods rely on fixed hyperparameters that may not generalize across different staleness levels and training stages.
Our work differs by targeting acceptance rate rather than variance directly, providing a principled way to automatically discover appropriate trajectory bounds without manual tuning.
However, these methods typically rely on fixed hyperparameters that require careful tuning for different staleness levels.

notes: Paper's own ablation attributes most of the improvement (+12.76pp) to tighter fixed bounds rather than the adaptive control itself; adaptive control is framed as providing 'automatic discovery of optimal settings'. Method is explicitly an extension/wrapper of MIS-PO (Huang et al., 2026).
